# Data Codebook

**Version: October 15, 2026.** Two balanced district-year panels; each contains 160
districts, seven study years, 1,120 rows, and the same nine columns. District and year
jointly identify a row. These are fully simulated data, not student records.

## Variables

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `district_id` | Integer district identifier, 1-160. Repeated across seven years. |
| `year` | Study year, 1-7; not an actual calendar year. |
| `cohort` | `treated_year5`, `treated_year6`, or `never`, as applicable. |
| `treatment_start_year` | First treated year. **0 means never treated.** |
| `treated_ever` | 1 for an eventually treated district; otherwise 0. |
| `treated` | 1 starting in the adoption year and in every subsequent year; otherwise 0. |
| `event_time` | `year - treatment_start_year` for eventually treated districts. Negative before adoption, zero at adoption. Missing for never-treated districts: `NA` in CSV, system missing `.` in Stata. |
| `outcome_std` | Continuous observed achievement on a common pre-treatment reference-SD scale. |
| `outcome_raw` | The same outcome in synthetic score points: `50 + 10 * outcome_std`. |

Only `event_time` has missing values, for never-treated districts. There are no
adjustment covariates and no generic `outcome` column. True effects and untreated
potential outcomes are kept separately for instructor validation.

## Design

| Dataset | Cohort | Districts | Post-treatment years |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Simulation 1 | Year 5 | 80 | 5, 6, 7 |
| Simulation 1 | Never treated | 80 | None |
| Simulation 2 | Year 5 | 40 | 5, 6, 7 |
| Simulation 2 | Year 6 | 40 | 6, 7 |
| Simulation 2 | Never treated | 80 | None |

The October 15 correction changes the former Year 7 adopters to never-treated
districts. The Year 5 and Year 6 assignments, untreated outcomes, and all seven
observation years are preserved. Simulation 1 is unchanged. There are no
student-level records or school-level rows in these teaching files.

Treatment is assigned at district level and never switches off. All districts are
untreated in Years 1-4. The new panels retain that pre-treatment structure, not the
exact numerical values of the previous 11-year version.

## Outcome Scale and Generation

The generator uses seed **20261014**, random district effects, a common year trend,
and district errors with AR(1) correlation 0.6. Cohort assignment is randomized
independently of these untreated outcomes. No district-specific slopes or covariates
enter the outcome model. This creates parallel untreated trends in expectation;
sample pre-trends need not coincide exactly. Treatment has no anticipation or spillovers.

The untreated outcome's pooled Years 1-4 mean and sample SD define a single reference
scale shared by both simulations. Treatment effects are added afterward. Thus the
observed `outcome_std` need not have mean zero or SD one after treatment. A difference
of 0.20 reference SD is exactly 2 raw score points.

The raw scale is an affine transformation, not an observed test instrument. Values
are continuous and unbounded; 50 is the pre-treatment reference mean and 10 its SD.

Simulation 1 adds 0.20 reference SD (2 points) in every treated period. Simulation 2
adds `0.10 + 0.10 * event_time + 0.05 * (treatment_start_year - 5)` reference SD
in treated periods only. These chosen effects illustrate heterogeneous treatment
effects; they are not estimates from a real education study.

| Simulation 2 cell | True effect in raw points | Simple ATT weight |
|---|---:|---|
| ATT(5,5) | 1.00 | 1/5 |
| ATT(5,6) | 2.00 | 1/5 |
| ATT(5,7) | 3.00 | 1/5 |
| ATT(6,6) | 1.50 | 1/5 |
| ATT(6,7) | 2.50 | 1/5 |

The true Simple ATT is 2 raw points. Sample estimates will differ because of
sampling noise. Earlier cohorts receive more total weight because more of their
post-treatment periods are observed. The Year 6 cohort is observed through event
time 1; only the Year 5 cohort contributes an effect at event time 2. These are
data-generating effects, not estimated model results. The Workshop page and
downloadable lab results use this corrected two-cohort design.
